steps.note: CISA lessons calls it a multi-year effort to gain the maintainer's trust, and the rsc timeline dates Jia Tan's first patch to 2021-10-29.
The rsc timeline names Jigar Kumar and Dennis Ens in June 2022 and says they were likely fakes, and Akamai says the attacker used fake accounts to pressure the maintainer.
The rsc timeline shows the GitHub org, commit access and first tagged release, and Tukaani confirms Jia Tan made and signed 5.6.0/5.6.1 and had the GitHub-hosted access.
The rsc timeline says Jia Tan merged the ifunc commit, turned ifunc off in OSS-Fuzz and pointed OSS-Fuzz bugs to themself, and JFrog backs this; 'reported' fits.
Freund says the obfuscated exploit sits in test files that no 5.6.0 test used, and the rsc timeline dates Jia Tan's commit to 2024-02-23.
Freund and the rsc timeline say the 5.6.0/5.6.1 tarballs held a modified build-to-host.m4 that is not in the git repository.
The rsc timeline records Jia Tan's Fedora 40 email and Ubuntu bug, and Hans Jansen's Debian bug for 5.6.1; 'reported' fits.
Freund describes the end-of-configure script, the x86-64 Linux, gcc, GNU ld and deb/rpm conditions, and his anti-investigation suspicion; the CVE record backs the liblzma change.
Freund says OpenSSH does not use liblzma directly, distro systemd-notify patches pull in libsystemd and liblzma, and RSA_public_decrypt is redirected.

Valsorda's analysis says the payload comes from the key's N value, is checked against a fixed Ed448 key and passed to system() before login, sshd otherwise acts normally, and no reliable scanner is possible.

covered.note: Matched by output build-trust (attacker earns trust from the victim project).
Matched by output pressure, the same sock-puppet campaign aimed at the maintainer and project.
Matched by output gain-access (commit and release rights, signed tarballs).
Matched by output weaken-fuzzing (ifunc turned off in OSS-Fuzz).
Matched by output hide-payload (obfuscated payload in binary test files).
Matched by output ship-tarballs (tampered build macro found only in release tarballs).
No output step says the backdoored versions were actually packaged by Debian testing or Fedora; lobby-distros covers only the push to adopt, and the spread appears only in impact.
Matched by output build-inject (a distro package build injects code into liblzma).
No output step covers the runtime environment and debugger checks on sshd hosts; build-inject covers only the build-time conditions.
Matched by output sshd-hook (liblzma via libsystemd hooks the sshd RSA check).
Matched by output key-gated (key-gated remote command execution on sshd).
